title: Orphaned-upload reaper: cron sweep for attachment rows never confirmed
objective: Reclaim storage objects and rows left behind when a signed-URL upload is issued but never confirmed. Without this, every abandoned upload is permanent litter in a private bucket nobody lists.
scope: Idempotent sweep deleting quote_attachments rows where confirmed_at IS NULL and uploaded_at is older than the upload-URL TTL (2h, fixed by Supabase), together with their storage objects
Registered as a Supabase Cron (pg_cron) job following the T-031 job patterns: schedule, purpose, idempotency key strategy, failure behaviour and observability expectations documented per CLAUDE.md
Must tolerate retries and duplicate delivery, and be safe to run concurrently with live uploads - a row younger than the TTL must never be reaped
out_of_scope: Changing the upload/confirm flow itself (T-027, PASS)
Shortening the upload-URL TTL - storage-js createSignedUploadUrl accepts no expiresIn, verified against installed 2.110.7
implementation_details: The ordering hazard is the whole task: reaping a row whose upload is still in flight destroys a legitimate upload. Assert the TTL boundary from BOTH sides (just-inside kept, just-outside reaped), not merely that old rows go.
Delete the storage object and the row together, and make the handler safe if the object is already gone - a partial previous run must be completable, not fatal.
Follow the T-031 cron/queue patterns rather than inventing a new one.

integration: A pending row older than the TTL is reaped with its object; one younger is NOT
Idempotency: running the sweep twice produces the same end state and the second run is a no-op
A row whose object is already deleted still completes
Confirmed and removed rows are never touched

history.message: Created by the orchestrator on evaluator finding F-027-2 while passing T-027. T-027 correctly flagged the gap rather than building an unscoped cron inside an attachments task. Depends on T-031 for the established job patterns as well as T-027.

Implemented the orphaned-upload-reaper cron sweep following the T-032/T-034 patterns. MEASURED vs assumed against the T-027 schema: aged against `uploaded_at` (not a separate created_at; uploaded_at is stamped at request time on the pending row and re-stamped at confirm); soft-remove column is `removed_at` (nullable pair with removed_by, NULL=present); confirmed marker is `confirmed_at` (NULL=pending). Candidate predicate = confirmed_at IS NULL AND removed_at IS NULL AND uploaded_at < (now - TTL); TTL defaults to SUPABASE_UPLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (7200s, the fixed Supabase upload-URL lifetime). Row delete reuses the existing `deletePendingAttachment` (guarded confirmed_at IS NULL) as defense-in-depth; object delete goes through the injected StorageAdapter, object-FIRST then row (the recoverable order, matching discardPendingAttachment). Files: src/server/jobs/cron/orphaned-upload-reaper.ts (handler + pure orphanUploadCutoff), src/server/domains/quotes/attachments.repository.ts (+listOrphanedAttachmentCandidates), quotes/index.ts (exports), jobs/cron/registry.ts (+CRON_JOB_NAMES entry), jobs/runtime.ts (builds StorageAdapter, registers handler), api/cron/orphaned-upload-reaper.ts (endpoint), supabase/migrations/20260720020000_pg_cron_orphaned_upload_reaper_schedule.sql ('30 * * * *' reusing invoke_cron_endpoint; commits NO url/secret). Tests: unit orphaned-upload-reaper-cutoff.test.ts (5, TTL/DST arithmetic), integration orphaned-upload-reaper-job.test.ts (8: exact reaped set, object+row deleted together, TTL boundary both sides incl. exact-boundary `<` vs `<=`, object-already-gone completes, confirmed+soft-removed never touched, idempotent second run reaps 0, two-tenant isolation, end-to-end dispatch via runCronJob writing a job_run row). Gates: typecheck 0, lint 0, db:types:check 0 (no schema-type change), full npm test 111 files / 3722 passed / 0 failed (floor 3706), cron:list reports orphaned-upload-reaper registered, pg-cron-schedules + cron-scripts suites green. Mutation evidence (binary-safe edits, restored byte-identical, sha256 verified): (1) `<`->`<=` in candidate query reaped orphanAtBoundary -> boundary test red; (2) dropped `removed_at IS NULL` clause reaped removedPendingOld -> soft-removed test red; (3) cutoff sign `-`->`+` -> 4 unit assertions red. Migration disclosure: added supabase/migrations/20260720020000_*; applied ONLY its additive `cron.schedule(...)` upsert to the live local DB (not a reset/db:validate) so pg-cron-schedules could observe it — orchestrator should review the diff and refresh the snapshot. No secret or URL committed (schedule reuses the out-of-band job_cron_config helper). No open findings.

PASS. First-hand verification (not taken on trust): (1) TTL boundary pinned from both sides by reading the integration fixture table directly — orphanJustOutside (cutoff-1min) reaped, orphanAtBoundary (cutoff exactly) kept, orphanJustInside (cutoff+1min) kept, proving `<` not `<=`. Reproduced the `<`->`<=` mutant on attachments.repository.ts's listOrphanedAttachmentCandidates myself (binary-mode Python edit): the boundary test and the two-tenant test went red exactly as claimed (orphanAtBoundary wrongly reaped); restored and verified sha256 identical to pre-mutation (ba4c4105b1053c1609b44332bbfbb7c4b84cde71b8c2c5105653b0d6f40b3283, matched before/after). (2) End-to-end deletion reproduced by running the 'dispatches through runCronJob...' test myself: it seeds a fresh orphan with a real fake-bucket object, runs the handler through runCronJob, and asserts both the DB row (0 rows) AND the storage object (storage.keys() no longer contains it) are gone, plus a job_run row with status=succeeded and counts containing attachmentsReaped — not merely a registry-name check. (3) Reproduced the removed_at-IS-NULL-dropped mutant myself (binary-mode Python edit to the same repository file): removedPendingOld was wrongly reaped, two tests went red; restored and verified sha256 identical (same hash as above). Predicate read directly from attachments.repository.ts: confirmed_at IS NULL AND removed_at IS NULL AND uploaded_at < uploadedBefore — matches claim exactly. (4) Idempotency: ran 'running the sweep twice reaps nothing the second time' myself — second run's attachmentsReaped/attachmentsFailed both 0, survivor rows and objects byte-for-byte unchanged; the 'completes when the object is already gone' test separately confirms tolerance. (5) Read the actual T-027 migrations (20260718003400_quote_attachments.sql, 20260719002100_quote_attachments_confirmed_at.sql) directly: confirmed no separate created_at column exists (uploaded_at is the only timestamp at insert), removed_at is the soft-remove column, confirmed_at is the pending marker (NULL=pending) — all measured claims check out. Confirmed SUPABASE_UPLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 7200 in supabase-adapter.ts. (6) Read the new migration file directly: contains only `cron.schedule('orphaned-upload-reaper', '30 * * * *', $cron$select public.invoke_cron_endpoint(...)$cron$)` — no extensions.http_* reference, no URL, no secret, confirming it reuses the T-032 helper rather than repeating its pg_net defect. Ran `npm run cron:list` myself: orphaned-upload-reaper reports 'registered'; traced run-cron.ts's --list path to createJobRuntime() (real registration, not a static name array) and registry.ts's `cronHandlers.get(name) !== undefined` check, which would report 'NOT REGISTERED' for any CRON_JOB_NAMES entry whose factory was not wired in runtime.ts — the overclaim guard is real, not merely asserted. The audit belongs to confirm') — this is consistent with established domain precedent, not a gap against AC-024's enumerated operation list (attachment add/remove refers to CONFIRMED attachments).
